title: Cross-implementation: each endpoint parses the other's envelopes; identical inputs give identical bytes

criteria.text: For every vector with inputs, Endpoint A and Endpoint B build the same bytes, equal to the vector file; for every receiver and SEC-B case both give the expected result and reason
criteria.measured: build: 36 items, A==B 36, A==expected 36, B==expected 36; receive: 23 items, A==B 23, A==expected 23, B==expected 23; sec_b: 34 items, A==B 34, A==expected 34, B==expected 34

criteria.text: Endpoint A's vector run passes every check
The comparison program finds no difference
details: receive   23 items: A == B  23, A == expected  23, B == expected  23
sec_b     34 items: A == B  34, A == expected  34, B == expected  34

criteria.text: Endpoint A decodes every envelope Endpoint B logged as sent (all have envelope_hex) with the same field values, and Endpoint B received every envelope A sent, byte-identical (the tool fails otherwise)
criteria.measured: a-crosscheck exit status 0; decoded 7 of 7 peer send records (0 without bytes), 0 field mismatches; own envelopes delivered 8 of 8, byte-identical 8

criteria.text: Endpoint B decodes every envelope Endpoint A logged as sent (all have envelope_hex) with the same field values, and Endpoint A received every envelope B sent, byte-identical (the tool fails otherwise)
criteria.measured: b-crosscheck exit status 0; decoded 8 of 8 peer send records (0 without bytes), 0 field mismatches; own envelopes delivered 7 of 7, byte-identical 7

criteria.text: Every envelope handed to ION is received by the other endpoint
Every received envelope is byte-identical to the envelope handed to ION
criteria.measured: 15 of 15 received envelopes byte-identical (SHA-256 and header)

criteria.text: Each endpoint accepts every envelope of the other implementation
The protected command with an unknown frame type is executed
